definitions.explanation: Formally including someone or something into an existing group, organization, or system. In education, it refers specifically to transferring into a school or university partway through the program.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}に{編入|へんにゅう}する。
{短大|たんだい}から{四年制|よねんせい}{大学|だいがく}の{三年次|さんねんじ}に{編入|へんにゅう}した。
examples.english: I transferred from a junior college into the third year of a four-year university.

examples.japanese: その{地域|ちいき}は{市町村|しちょうそん}{合併|がっぺい}により{隣|となり}の{市|し}に{編入|へんにゅう}された。
examples.english: That area was incorporated into the neighboring city through a municipal merger.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in educational contexts as {編入|へんにゅう}{学|がく} (transfer admission) or {編入|へんにゅう}{試験|しけん} (transfer entrance exam). Also used in administrative and military contexts for incorporating units or territories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {編入|へんにゅう}{試験|しけん}: transfer entrance examination
- {編入|へんにゅう}{学|がく}: transfer enrollment
- ～に{編入|へんにゅう}する: to be incorporated into
- {三年次|さんねんじ}{編入|へんにゅう}: third-year transfer
